newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil, Brent called down on bearish API data.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil, Brent called down on bearish API data.

text.p: IPE gas oil and Brent crude oil were called to open substantially lower on Wednesday following bearish weekly U.S. stock figures from the American Petroleum Institute (API), brokers said.

May gas oil was called to open down $2-$3 from Tuesday's close at $165.25 a tonne while the prompt June Brent contract was due to start on Wednesday, down some 15-25 cents from Tuesday's $18.14 a barrel close.
"The API's are bearish all round. We'll see support levels broken. There just was nothing positive there at all,' one broker commented.
API's showed a build on crude of 2.97 million barrels, on gasoline of 3.63 million barrels and on distillates of 2.59 million barrels.
June Brent on SIMEX had lost some 18 cents to trade at $17.96 a barrel by 0745 GMT.
Support on the prompt June Brent crude contract at $17.80 should be broken in the morning session, brokers added.
"These numbers are too bearish for that level to hold. I don't know how low we will go," one said.
May WTI crude on ACCESS lost some 23 cents to trade at $19.60 a barrel by 0753 GMT.
"We're watching to see if the $19.50 support holds. If not we could drop quite a bit," he added. --Siobhan Hayden London Newsroom +44 171 542 8978
